findings.title: `_read_turn` signature exceeds the project's 88-character line limit
findings.description: The line `async def _read_turn(self, turns: DispatchTurns, *, idle_s: float | None) -> ResultMessage | None:` is ~99 characters, over the 88-char limit enforced by the project's ruff `E` rules. Everything else in the changed files I inspected respects the limit. Trivial mechanical fix.

findings.title: Abandoned async generator on idle-timeout path
findings.description: When `asyncio.timeout(idle_s)` fires, `_read_turn` is cancelled mid-`anext` and the `aiter(self.client.receive_response())` generator created in that frame is never `aclose()`d; control returns to `_collect_turns`, which builds a fresh generator on the next `receive_response()` call. This is fine for the `ScriptedClient` fake, and plausibly fine for the real SDK (a new `receive_response()` call is the documented recovery), but nothing here guarantees the cancelled generator is finalized promptly — it relies on GC. If the SDK's generator holds transport state, a `finally: await stream.aclose()`-style cleanup (guarded) would make the failure mode explicit rather than implicit. Not blocking; the observable signals (WARNING logs, `background_tasks_stopped` counters) for the timeout path are all present and tested.
